text:
marcus: Ok team — proposal for a tighter quant-benchmark protocol so we can reduce run-to-run variance and make kernel selection apples-to-apples. TL;DR: deterministic tokenization, explicit KV priming, fixed warmup tokens, power cap + P-state pinned, and single-run kernel traces.

sana: sounds good. can you list the exact steps?

marcus: sure. draft protocol below. feedback welcome.

jonah: quick Q: do we enforce a single GPU model config per variant (eg same #streams)? important for batching heuristics.

marcus: yes — we pin streams/threads. protocol step summary: 
1) Env pinning: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, tf/cuda cudnn flags, and set NET_TRAINER_THREADS=1
2) Tokenization: use tokenizer v2.3.1 and run with --seed 42 to ensure deterministic offsets
3) KV priming: run 128 tokens of warmup per prompt to populate KV cache; for cache-sensitive tests also run a cold-run with 0 priming
4) Warmup iterations: run 30 warmup sequences (seq_len=512) *before* measuring latency and throughput.
5) Power and P-state: use nvidia-smi to set power cap and nvidia-smi -ac to pin clocks where applicable. record power cap in metadata
6) Batching: evaluate at single-request, batch sizes [2,4,8] with the same arrival spacing distribution (poisson with lambda=0.2)
7) Kernel tracing: enable kernel selector logs and NVTX zones for the measured interval only
8) Calibration note: when comparing INT8/FP8/4bit, run calibration on the same dataset (50k tokens) and save both scale/zero params and a checksum of the calibration outputs
9) Repeat: run each configuration 5 independent times and report mean/median/stddev.

olivia: for KV priming, recommend using a set of 20 diverse prompts instead of random text — helps catch corner-cases in KV addressing.

sam: observed a weird perf regression yesterday in FP8 on the 70B variant — kernels switched from fp16_attention to fp8_attention_conv and latency jumped ~18% despite lower FLOP count. I'll paste logs.

sam: ```
[profile] model=llama-70b-q8: kernel=fp8_attention_conv
avg_token_ms=15.3
median_token_ms=12.8
kv_hit_rate=0.88
selected_kernel_trace=[fp8_attention_conv, int8_matmul_opt, kv_lookup_fast]
```

erica: oof. did you check cache alignment? FP8 kernels assume 64B alignment for packed weights otherwise memcpy overhead.

sam: i did see an extra memcpy in the kernel timeline. on P4 it was tiny but on A100 it was visible. seems to be a codepath for misaligned quant blocks.

jonah: let's add an alignment verification step to the protocol: after calibration, run `tools/align_check.py --model <path>` and fail the run if any block != 64 bytes.

marcus: good call. also adding: always record the calibration checksum + weight packing checksum in the run metadata. that way we can diff failing runs quickly.

bench-bot: CI job posted: https://ci.internal/bench/quant/1738274562 — artifacts include nvprof traces, kernel selector logs, and calibration blobs.

olivia: another subtle source of variance: tokenizer pretokenization step using SSE vs scalar fallback. we should force the same build flags for tokenizers across machines (eg disable AVX512 fallback on older nodes).

marcus: adding that to env pinning: TOKENIZER_BUILD_TAG=avx2 to lock behavior.

sam: sample run command i used:
```
./bench/run_quant.sh \
  --model-path models/llama-70b \
  --qtype fp8 \
  --calib-data data/calib-50k.jsonl \
  --warmup 30 \
  --seq-len 512 \
  --kv-prime 128 \
  --power-cap 250 \
  --pin-pstate 0x1F \
  --tokenizer-version 2.3.1 \
  --rng-seed 42 \
  --out artifacts/1738274562
```

erica: for fairness we should also capture microstate: current GPU SM utilization, memory bandwidth, and L2 hit rate (from nvprof/nvtx). put these in a CSV in artifacts.

marcus: agreed. suggested artifact layout: artifacts/<run>/metadata.json (includes power cap, tokenizer tag, checksums), artifacts/<run>/nvprof.nvtx, artifacts/<run>/kernels.log, artifacts/<run>/calib.blob, artifacts/<run>/align_report.txt, artifacts/<run>/micro.csv

jonah: what about cold-cache vs hot-cache comparison? we might be unfairly favoring KV-primed runs for some models.

marcus: include both: every config produces both a cold-run (no priming) and hot-run (128 priming). label them. benchmark report should show both curves.

sam: one more: random seed affects deterministic sampling for tokenizers (esp. for byte-pair merges). set FASTBPE_SEED=0 to force deterministic merges.

olivia: can we add an automatic kernel-chooser replay: take the nvprof trace and run it through kernel-selector to validate that chosen kernels match expected heuristics? helps detect selector regressions.

marcus: yes — adding post-check `tools/verify_kernel_choice.py --trace nvprof.nvtx --policy expected_policy.yaml`

erica: final ask — please add a one-paragraph summary in each run describing any divergence between calibration stats (scale/zero) and production-run stats (activation ranges). big mismatches indicate calibration distribution drift.

marcus: thanks everyone. i'll update the repo with a `docs/benchmarking/quant_protocol.md` and land the CI job template. plan to run a baseline sweep tomorrow and open an RFC if we see persistent kernel-switch regressions. :thumbsup:

sana: thanks — this will make our comparatives much cleaner.
